Name: Opposing the practice of federal immigration authorities using parking facilities as staging locations for enforcement actions anywhere in the five boroughs and calling on private operators to refuse participation
Title: Resolution opposing the practice of federal immigration authorities using parking facilities as staging locations for enforcement actions anywhere in the five boroughs and calling on private operators to refuse participation

History.Description: This Resolution was Introduced by Council
This Resolution was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Immigration

Text:
Whereas, Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, federal immigration authorities, including United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), have been violently and aggressively terrorizing communities across the United States; and
Whereas, Federal immigration authorities have increased their scale of immigration enforcement operations, expanded their racial profiling, and intensified their use of violent force, the latter of which resulted in the fatal shootings by federal immigration authorities of Renée Good and Alex Pretti in Minnesota; and
Whereas, ICE activity has torn immigrant families apart, instilled fear in communities subjected to their operations, kept immigrants from accessing basic services, and made day to day life feel unsafe for so many; and
Whereas, Prior to enacting an operation, ICE and other federal immigration authorities have seemingly relied on parking lots as staging sites; and
Whereas, In Chicago, as immigration enforcement operations took place under Operation Midway Blitz, Mayor Johnson signed an executive order prohibiting federal immigration agents from using any City-owned property in their operations after it was documented that ICE used City-owned lots as staging sites for operations; and
Whereas, In Minneapolis, Mayor Frey signed a similar executive order prohibiting federal immigration authorities from using municipal parking lots, vacant lots, and garages as staging grounds for enforcement operations; and
Whereas, In New York City, Mayor Mamdani signed Executive Order 13 which similarly prohibited federal immigration agents from entering city property, including municipal parking garages and lots, without a judicial warrant; and
Whereas, In New York City, with the prohibition of federal immigration agents from City-owned lots, ICE has reportedly turned their attention to private parking lots; and
Whereas, In April 2026, ICE posted a procurement notice looking for up to 150 parking spaces in Hudson Square near their Varick Street field office; and
Whereas, However, federal immigration authorities seemingly had arrangements with other private operators throughout the City or were informally using private lots; and
Whereas, In April 2026, it was reported by Documented that ICE had been using bank parking lots along Northern Boulevard in Queens as informal staging points; and
Whereas, In May 2026, an arrangement made between federal immigration authorities and a garage on Morton Street in Manhattan was terminated after residents organized and contacted the garage company directly; and
Whereas, In August 2026, residents protested suspected ICE parking in a garage on Harrison Street in Tribeca; and
Whereas, At the end of June 2026, Hudson River Park Trust’s contract with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) lapsed after significant public pressure, but according to local organizers, there were four suspected ICE vehicles parked in the lot after the contract ended; and
Whereas, Prior to ICE’s recent operation and shooting of Oscar Belgal in Marble Hill, it was reported that ICE agents were using a private parking lot a few blocks away for staging operations; and
Whereas, According to Gothamist, residents of Marble Hill had reportedly warned for months that ICE was using a local commercial parking lot as a staging ground; and
Whereas, After the Marble Hill shooting, Mayor Mamdani and over 100 elected officials called on parking garage owners and operators to keep ICE off their properties; and
Whereas, After reports of ICE using City-owned property for parking in Van Cortlandt Park in the Bronx and along 111th Street on the west side of Flushing Meadows Corona Park in Queens, Mayor Mamdani sent a letter to DHS demanding ICE cease this activity and threatened legal action if ICE continued to park in City-owned lots; and
Whereas, Immigrant New Yorkers deserve to experience this City without fear and New York City must not facilitate the current lawlessness of federal immigration authorities; now, therefore, be it
Resolved, That the Council of the City of New York opposes the practice of federal immigration authorities using parking facilities as staging locations for enforcement actions anywhere in the five boroughs and calling on private operators to refuse participation.
